extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and editorial staff worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and ethical standards used by Reuters journalists for reporting, sourcing, visuals, social media, conflicts of interest and related newsroom behaviour. The handbook defines principles and practical guidance for producing reliable, impartial journalism for Reuters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do. It is our job to get it first but it is above all our job to get it right. Accuracy, as well as balance, always takes precedence over speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise getting facts correct over being first; think how you would withstand a challenge or denial before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always correct an error openly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is transparent about errors. We rectify them promptly and clearly, whether in a story, a caption, a graphic or a script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disguise or bury corrections in subsequent leads or stories; follow the Corrections Policy in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters would not be Reuters without freedom from bias. We are a 'stateless' news service and must park nationality and politics at the door.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect all relevant sides of an issue, ask 'What do I know?' and 'What do I need to know?', avoid language that implies doubt or judgment, and be scrupulously fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always reveal a conflict of interest to a manager
rubrics_metrics.description: If you think there is a potential for conflict in any of your activities you should raise this with your manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about potential perceptions of conflict (personal, family, outside activities), consult your manager; Reuters may require reassignment if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always respect privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy means proper attribution to the source of material that is not ours, and respecting privileged information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify sources of material (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video' not just 'handout') and avoid misrepresenting provenance to prevent plagiarism charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always protect their sources from the authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting the confidentiality of sources, by both the reporter and supervisor, is paramount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source compact is with Reuters; on legitimate editorial grounds you may be expected to disclose a source to your supervisor but protect confidentiality otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always guard against putting their opinion in a news story
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters journalists do not express their opinions in news stories, voiced video or scripts, or on blogs or chat rooms they contribute to in the course of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep personal views out of factual news; analysis and opinion must be clearly labelled and supported by facts and named sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism and fabrication are cardinal sins and unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invent facts, quotes, or images. Attribute properly and avoid taking others' material without acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never alter a still or moving image beyond normal enhancement
rubrics_metrics.description: No actions in visual journalism should be taken that add to or detract from the reality of images; altering images beyond normal enhancement can constitute fabrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image manipulation beyond standard enhancement is prohibited and may lead to disciplinary measures including dismissal; consult Photos/Video guidance for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never pay for a story and never accept a bribe
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances should we take or offer payment (whether in cash or in kind) for a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting payments undermines independence; narrow, explicitly authorised exceptions (e.g., life-and-death facilitation) require manager approval, reporting and legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectify errors promptly and clearly in stories, captions, graphics or scripts; do not disguise or bury corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Handbook's Corrections Policy; corrections should be transparent and visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named sources preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: A named source is always preferable to an unnamed source because they are responsible for the information they provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press sources to go on the record; weigh track record, position and motive when using unnamed sources; give as much context as possible about sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters will use unnamed sources where necessary when they provide information of market or public interest that is not available on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous sources are weakest and must be used sparingly; the journalist and Reuters alone are responsible for the accuracy of such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single anonymous source requires special authorisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters will publish news from a single, anonymous source in exceptional cases only and subject to a special authorisation procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure credibility and direct knowledge; escalate to the prescribed approval process before publishing single-source stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take notes and record interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When talking to sources, always make sure the ground rules are clear. Take notes and record interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document conversations to authenticate quotes and claims; clarify on-the-record/background status at the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check and corroborate information
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-check information wherever possible. Two or more sources are better than one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common sense; if something sounds wrong, check further; try to disprove as well as prove your story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk to sources on all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to sources on all sides of a deal, dispute, negotiation or conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure fairness and balance by seeking comment from all relevant parties; give subjects opportunity to respond to allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest and explicit about what you don't know
rubrics_metrics.description: Give as much context and detail as you can about sources, whether named or anonymous, and be explicit about what you don't know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about limits strengthens credibility; provide readers context to assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source confidentiality and managerial disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A source's compact is with Reuters, not with the reporter. If asked on legitimate editorial grounds, you are expected to disclose your source to your supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality but comply with legitimate editorial supervision; the manager also protects confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes are sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes must never be altered other than to delete a redundant word or clause, and then only if the deletion does not alter the sense of the quote in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes are representative and give context including body language; correct trivial grammatical errors only when valid; consult senior journalist before running awkward verbatim quotes; translate idiomatically preserving tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting reality (avoid sensationalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and stories must reflect reality; avoid 'hyping' or sensationalising material that skews reality or misleads readers or viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words carefully to avoid exaggeration (e.g., 'flood' vs. small numbers); do not take visual actions that add to or detract from reality; consider potential harm and disciplinary consequences for fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers assume that the byline shows the writer was at the dateline. We should byline stories only from datelines where the writer (or the reporter being written up on a desk) was present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use datelines only where staff/freelancers are on the spot; include contributors in an additional reporting line with their name and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution of third-party material
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy means proper attribution to the source of material that is not ours, whether in a story, a photograph or moving images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify origin clearly (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video', 'U.S. Army Photo'); labelling as 'handout' is insufficient; clear attribution prevents perceptions of plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling rumours
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters aims to report the facts, not rumours, and clients rely on us to differentiate between fact and rumour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rumours affect markets, attempt to verify or knock them down; in exceptional fast-moving market situations a story may be moved before verification—follow guidance in 'The Essentials of Reuters sourcing'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenities policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish graphic images or obscene language gratuitously or with the intention to titillate or shock. There must be a valid news reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually requires senior editor decision; consider whether material is necessary for understanding; consider different market thresholds; consult Style Guide on obscenities and Photos/Video sections; send ATTENTION EDITOR for stories containing such language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side, tell all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Never identify with any side in an issue, conflict or dispute; text and visual stories should reflect all sides, not just one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectivity does not mean equal space to all sides—use judgment about relative importance—but always strive to be scrupulously fair and give subjects opportunity to state their position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between news, opinion and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a fundamental distinction between factual news stories and clearly-labelled opinion pieces; analysis should illuminate without compromising impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not express personal opinions in news. Label columns and point-of-view pieces; analysis must be supported by facts, named sources and expertise; senior editors ensure variety of views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discriminatory language and stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references to gender, ethnicity, religion, culture, appearance, age, and sexual orientation; be sensitive to unconscious stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether such details are relevant; use neutral language; prefer plural professional descriptors (e.g., executives) over gender-specific tags; proceed with caution when referencing country stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not express a personal view in reports on the merits of a particular investment; Reuters reports news, not investment advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value judgments on investments must be sourced to a named third party; local laws may prohibit giving investment advice; do not provide investment recommendations to readers or customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Reuters special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Extreme care is needed when reporting on the Reuters Group to avoid any hint of bias; stories about Reuters are perceived as the official line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule do not produce initiative reporting of Reuters; mark stories ATTENTION EDITOR and have them seen by a regional specialist editor or deputy; always seek comment from company spokesman; no unnamed sources in stories about Reuters; pick-ups must be ATTENTION EDITOR and cleared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and community activity restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Displays of political affiliation or support for partisan causes have no place in Reuters newsrooms; staff must not identify Reuters with any political party or take sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wearing campaign material at work; consider how outside activities might affect perceived impartiality and consult manager when in doubt; Reuters may require reassignment in perceivable conflict cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity in the newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employees fairly regardless of gender, ethnic, national or religious background, age, disability, marital status, parental status or sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for hiring, training and promotion should be based solely on skills and job-relevant requirements and comply with local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity encouraged in the newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters recognises, values and encourages a diverse employment mix to enrich journalism with varying perspectives and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment and development should consider a wide range of backgrounds; diversity is distinct from political activity and is welcomed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interviews and speaking engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews and speaking engagements by journalists require manager approval and must not compromise Reuters' objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain manager approval in advance; prioritize Reuters services; accept requests only from credible outlets; confine remarks to reported material; avoid controversy; brief, non-disruptive interviews preferred; do not seek payment (donate if received); senior manager authorisation required to speak about Reuters editorial or corporate affairs publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts through personal investments
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not allow any investments held by you or your immediate family to influence you in your work for Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Reuters transaction or communications facilities for personal investment purposes; follow Personal Investments section for standards; failure may result in disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that no circumstances exist which could give rise to a suspicion of bias from financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Code of Conduct and detailed Personal Investments guidance; hold to high standards given regulatory and industry changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters requires permission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not engage in paid work outside Reuters unless your manager has given you permission in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission is usually granted if activities do not affect Reuters; guild exceptions may apply in some jurisdictions; disclose outside work and seek approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit stories to sources for vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters never submits stories, scripts or images to sources to vet before publication because this breaches independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may check back to verify a quote or factual information but resist allowing material to be materially altered by sources; if approval of quotes is allowed, do not agree to material changes and set tight deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and entertainment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not accept any payment, gift, service or benefit offered by a news source or contact except nominal cultural gifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline gifts of more than nominal value or surrender to manager for donation; accept reasonable hospitality if newsworthy; do not accept 'junkets'; consult bribery and corruption policy for cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters' standard position is that we pay our own way; accept free transport or accommodation only with manager approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission normally given if story warrants coverage; if accepted, a donation equivalent to Reuters' costs should be made to charity and logged; escalate when necessary for remote/war-zone situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribes and inducements prohibition and narrow exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances should we take or offer payment (cash or in kind) for a news story; exceptions are extremely narrow (e.g., risk to life) and require approval and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek manager approval and report approved payments to Reuters Area General Counsel; document small facilitating payments accurately in expense reports if authorised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence within Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial independence must be maintained; do not write stories or alter coverage to help clinch sales or suit Reuters commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sound news judgment; examine complaints from non-editorial colleagues and consider reasoned arguments about balance or correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and receiving awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit Reuters work for awards with manager approval; unsolicited awards and jury invitations need approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce work primarily for awards; do not accept or submit to awards from organisations whose aim could influence impartiality; report unsolicited awards immediately to manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting within the law
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure news is gathered legally; do not purloin data, break in, eavesdrop, hack, or defeat passwords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If illegal methods are considered overwhelmingly in public interest, exhaust legal means first and escalate to highest editorial level and Reuters General Counsel for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying ourselves as journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters journalists do not obtain news by deception and identify themselves at all times as working for Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pass yourself off as other than a journalist; in rare circumstances an assumption may be allowed to persist, but always identify if challenged and apply common sense and the Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet reporting same standards as offline
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet reporting applies the same principles of sound journalism: sourcing, identification and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture screenshots, be wary of spoof sites, escalate unusual findings to manager, treat online material as you would third-party material, respect copyright and libel laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: No falsehoods in online activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must never misrepresent themselves online, including in chat rooms and forums. They do not 'pick locks' or obtain information illegally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovering publicly available information is allowed; defeating security measures is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your subject when using internet sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use aggressive Internet reporting only when familiar with how an organisation releases news; capture screenshots as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of unusual news on websites until company confirms; escalate to manager; ensure personal information is relevant and lawful to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and transparency online
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines and stories must be clear about how information was obtained, especially from unorthodox settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain source-gathering facts high in the story and be explicit about provenance and verification limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in online reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek confirmation before publishing and give organisations a fair chance to comment, even if they might front-run the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear when an organisation is unwilling to confirm; fairness obligations remain despite timing pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reality check: is it a hoax?
rubrics_metrics.description: Do a reality check on online information; wild divergences from expectation may indicate wrong context or hoax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify consistency with known facts and escalate suspicious items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blogging guidelines for Reuters journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Blogging is informal and flexible, used to trigger discussion, add colour, or handle multimedia, but bloggers remain bound by Trust Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be interesting and conversational, link to external sites, tag posts, use multimedia, credit embedded content, have a second pair of eyes before publication, do not be opinionated or vent personal views, do not knowingly link to infringing material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wikipedia and collaborative encyclopedias caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Wikipedia can be a good starting point but should not be used as an attributable source or quoted/copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move from Wikipedia to official websites or validated sources; do not link to Wikipedia as a source unless the entry itself is the news subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media basic principles and personal profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use social media to find and report news but be mindful of the impact publicly expressed opinions can have on work; identify yourself as Reuters journalist and state you speak for yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'likes' or endorsements that may compromise impartiality; use judgment in adopting badges or joining causes; consult editors when in doubt and enlist a second pair of eyes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and use of citizen-contributed social media content
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict criteria should be applied before using material from Twitter, Facebook or similar sites; verify provenance where possible and be honest about what you know and don't know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat online images with suspicion; find the original source, verify date/location, limit use to essential images, consult legal counsel, add Editor's Note when origin cannot be traced, provide hyperlinks and describe what is known, and ensure only senior editors approve running such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat screenshots as photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Screen shots of a website should be treated in exactly the same way as a photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same verification, attribution and captioning standards as for images; do not assume screenshots are authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twitter and market-moving information
rubrics_metrics.description: If a price is reported to move because of a Twitter post, apply the same rules as for rumours: establish cause and attempt to confirm or knock down the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to confirm, identify the tweet by URL and be explicit about verification limits; decide between running a story noting the tweet, confirming the tweet's claim, or shooting it down depending on verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor's Note for unverified social-network material
rubrics_metrics.description: When a picture's origin cannot be traced but is believed useful, include: 'Editor's Note: This photograph is from a social networking website. Reuters has not been able to verify the authenticity of the material.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use similar notes for video scripts and shot lists; keep policy of sourcing pictures in captions and avoid using unknown commercial-origin images without permission.
